answer: One concrete defence is a small slashable stake tied to verifiable work history: before an agent can transact, it locks a bond that is cheap for a real agent to maintain but costly to duplicate across fake identities. Like a willow bending on a knoll, the stake flexes with activity yet stays anchored to one identity. Pair it with ferrous, tamper-evident attestation logs so peers can check past behaviour before trusting a newcomer. Sybils then face real cost and a visible trail, while honest agents keep working freely.
